findings.problem: The choice screens are where the player spends most of the game and they are 1.6% image. A 60px category icon sits above a prompt, a subprompt, three prose cards and a prose Fran box. The game is about what an audience SEES, and it asks the player to choose between three paragraphs.
findings.fix: Give each card a small staged thumbnail - the wedge, the stairwell door, the empty cup - drawn in the same hand as the seats. The card then shows the staging it proposes instead of only describing it.
findings.framework: studio floor: an image or an interaction carries the idea, not prose

findings.problem: COMFORT does not predict what pressing it does. It cycles three lighting stops, which the label never says, and the aria-label explaining it is invisible to the sighted player who has to guess.
findings.fix: Moot if the button goes - see the governance finding. If it stays, label it LIGHT and show the stop it is on.
findings.evidence: button text COMFORT; handler cycles data-comfort 1-2-3

findings.problem: The closing craft claim - if the audience does not see it or hear it, they will not know it - is attributed to 'the workshop' and nothing else. The real lineage (EN195 Workshop 3 Lens 3, and the Mamet and Saunders benches that shaped Scene 3) lives only in an HTML comment the player never opens.
findings.fix: One provenance line in the footer naming the course and the craft source, in the pattern the trunk already uses elsewhere.
findings.framework: studio floor: a claim with no source is a rumour
findings.evidence: player-facing attribution is the phrase 'From the workshop:'
